workflow.title: Review developer caches before using MacOSCleaner
workflow.primaryIntent: Help an Apple Silicon developer distinguish rebuildable cache from project dependencies and original data, and choose review/deletion method before cleanup.
workflow.leadDirection: Start with compatibility and a reversible-vs-direct-removal distinction, not promised gigabytes. Explain that a scan result is a candidate, not permission.
outline: Check macOS 26+ and Apple Silicon before choosing the tool
Identify the owning tool, rebuild/download cost and active work
Separate direct-pruned caches from Trash-based workflows
Use scan risk badges and review categories; never treat AI verdict as a guarantee
When local on-device explanations fit, and when recurring-growth investigation may fit Breathing Room
Record a baseline and recheck without calling Trash movement measured recovery
workflow.distinctFromComparison: Cache decision workflow and rebuild costs; comparison stays a short selection matrix, not a duplicate article.
workflow.visualPlan: After lead: official Cleanup app image only once cleared. Later: selected Breathing Room Space example-data preview with full disclosure. No invented scans or savings.
workflow.interactionHandoff: A non-executing checklist: owner known? original or regenerable? active project? backup/rebuild available? method direct removal or Trash? Unknown answers stop the decision. No filesystem access, cleanup button or guessed storage calculator.
workflow.toolLink: Relevant cache/rebuild checklist if implemented and verified; do not invent a working route.
workflow.requiredDisclosure: Breathing Room, which we build; source documentation, not hands-on testing.
